Hypothesis: Global attention can bridge low-density gaps and rearrange local geometry.
Evidence: Gap occupancy rises by 38.2% in Breast Cancer and 117.4% in Digits. Global attention retains fewer neighbours than local attention in all four datasets.

Hypothesis: Blocking cross-gap relations always preserves attention as a valid state-transition operator.
Evidence: Across three discrete graphs, mixing adjacency rows produces non-edge mass, self-loops and asymmetry even under an observed-neighbour mask. Meeting safety thresholds requires N_eff close to 1.

Hypothesis: Local compression scale can define a data-derived relation scale.
Evidence: Elastic local distances produce repeated gains across four classification datasets and Diabetes regression, especially in sparse regions.

Hypothesis: Adding higher-order acceleration and jerk features improves modelling.
Evidence: Long spring traces, higher-order differences and enforced acceleration penalties repeatedly overfit or reduce performance.

Hypothesis: A scale trace is more informative than one fixed local scale.
Evidence: Datasets prefer different k values. Direct averaging can reduce performance; routing among scale families is more stable.

Hypothesis: Uneven training density should always trigger inverse-density loss weighting.
Evidence: Simple inverse-density weights are unstable across datasets and slightly reduce Diabetes regression performance.

Hypothesis: Structural learning and occurrence frequency should be treated separately.
Evidence: Diabetes BMI coverage balancing reduces macro-RMSE from 65.43 to 60.22 and overall RMSE from 64.01 to 63.37.

Hypothesis: Wrapper exhaustion can guide replacement of attention aggregation.
Evidence: Karate, Davis and Florentine retain state violations under admissible neighbour relations; the tested safe settings have N_eff close to 1.

Hypothesis: A diagnostic requires interpretation under the target mechanism before selecting an action.
Evidence: BMI, s4 and age respond differently to coverage balancing. Natural RMSE and macro-RMSE also support different decisions on the same data.

Hypothesis: Structural learning can be separated from prevalence and followed by output calibration.
Evidence: Balanced Digits training improves balanced accuracy and recall but raises log-loss. Prevalence calibration recovers about 80% of the additional log-loss.
Biased sampling reduces peripheral Digits accuracy from 93.13% to 86.99%; oracle inverse-propensity weighting restores it only to 87.59%.

Hypothesis: Attention may score proposals while another operation generates admissible discrete states.
Evidence: Global discrete projection restores valid graph form. Relation-only edge gating preserves observed support and symmetry; binary state generation remains a separate requirement.

Hypothesis: Operator selection should reflect state constraints, relation order and the hypothesized mechanism.
Evidence: Davis path orders 1, 2 and 4 give AUC 0.500 for missing cross-partition edges. Three hops give 0.753; degree-normalized three-hop relations give 0.806.

Hypothesis: Insufficient relation evidence is a valid decision outcome.
Evidence: Florentine candidates are weak across 100 edge-recovery splits, mostly with AUC approximately 0.43–0.60. The graph has limited cycle redundancy and clustering.

Hypothesis: Mechanism diagnostics can directly specify the final operation before downstream results are inspected.
Evidence: ModeChoice, RAND HIE and Les Misérables improve on their principal metrics. Forced coverage correction fails on Engel, favouring candidate generation followed by selection.

Hypothesis: A diagnostic can be equated directly with an action.
Evidence: Despite uneven Engel coverage, forced balancing raises macro-RMSE from 130.08 to 135.07. A nested probe chooses the unchanged model in 63 of 80 outer splits.

Hypothesis: An unchanged baseline and abstention must be formal candidates.
Evidence: The Engel probe selects ordinary training in 78.75% of outer splits and substantially reduces the loss from automatic correction.

Hypothesis: Diagnostics should identify admissible losses and candidate families before a precise algorithm is selected.
Evidence: RAND HIE deviance improves by only about 0.067% under Poisson modelling, with variance about seven times the mean. ModeChoice improves NLL while accuracy is nearly unchanged.
